title: Weekly train conductor: tagging, gating, telemetry-driven rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a deterministic weekly release conductor ("train conductor") that produces candidate RC tags, evaluates a heartbeat of production telemetry against gating rules, and drives automated rollouts with safe, observable rollback. The goal is to replace ad-hoc cut scripts with a single service that: 1) computes canonical RC candidates from commit fingerprints and normalized changelogs, 2) runs pre- and post-cut gating checks (unit/integration smoke + synthetic latency/error thresholds), 3) orchestrates phased cohort rollouts, and 4) triggers automated rollback when telemetry crosses defined thresholds. This ticket focuses on the weekly build slice, RC naming policy, gating definitions, runbook automation, and telemetry hooks required for safe, one-button rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor service produces deterministic RC tags for weekly build slice using commit fingerprint and changelog hash
Gating rules executed automatically for every candidate: smoke tests, e2e canaries, and telemetry heartbeat check
Console shows rollout progress with per-cohort latency/error deltas and a one-click rollback action that runs automated mitigation steps
Release notes artifact synthesized automatically and attached to the tag (changelog normalization + PR links)
Playbook documented in Confluence and integrated into oncall runbooks for LTS channels
End-to-end tests for rollback flow (inject anomaly -> rollback -> verify recovery) added to CI
work_log: 2026-02-25: Kickoff meeting. Agreed scope: deterministic tag format, heartbeat gating, phased rollout, rollback automation. Attendees: Asha, Rafael, Mei Lin, Jordan.
2026-03-01: Prototype tag format chosen: v{semver}+train.{YYYYMMDD}.{slice}.{fingerprint}. Rationale: semantic version preserved for downstream consumers, train metadata appended for traceability.
2026-03-03: Decision: telemetry heartbeat will be a 3-minute sliding window of P95 latency, error-rate, and request-per-second. Thresholds versioned per release canal (stable vs LTS stricter).
2026-03-05: Implemented initial tagging lambda and changelog normalizer. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-conductor/pull/117
2026-03-07: Built console rollout UI skeleton and telemetry panel. Mock dashboard wired to staging metrics. Design feedback queued (DES-412).
2026-03-09: Integration with synthetic canary runner complete. Canary job runs for each candidate and reports results to conductor. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/canary-runner/pull/29

2026-03-11: Started work on rollback automation steps: route shift, capacity drain, and traffic split revert. Trade-off: immediate full rollback vs staged rollback; decided prefer staged rollback with an emergency full-cut path.

2026-03-12: Ran rehearsal on staging: created candidate tag, executed gating, started cohort rollout, injected 5% latency increase in cohort 2, verified rollback path successfully restored baseline. Runbook updated with operator checklist: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Train+Conductor+Runbook
notes: Tag naming: include changelog fingerprint to ensure identical candidate tags for given commit range even if branch names differ.
Gating policy: start conservative for LTS lanes (P95 delta < 5% and error-rate delta < 0.05%) and more permissive for experimental lanes.
Telemetry cost trade-off: heartbeat window kept short (3m) to reduce noise but paired with aggregated 1h rollups for postmortem analysis.
Rollback strategy: default to staged rollback (reverse cohorts) and provide emergency-rollback toggle that reverts traffic to previous stable tag and triggers autoscaling warmup.
Future work: integrate canary ML (anomaly detection) to surface non-threshold failures and tie into automated mitigation suggestions (ENG-XXXXX).
